text: With the GL-level reports covered, Chapter 6 now moves module by module through the operational reports a consultant produces most often, starting with Payables.

The Payables Invoice Aging Report lists unpaid invoices by aging bucket, current, one to thirty days past due, thirty-one to sixty, sixty-one to ninety, over ninety. This is the formal, often scheduled counterpart to the ad hoc OTBI aging analysis from lesson eleven, same question, different tool and purpose.

Reading it well means looking beyond the total. A large "over ninety" bucket relative to total payables means a cash flow problem, a supplier dispute, or a data problem, an invoice that should've been paid or cancelled. Each needs a different next action, which is why you actually read the report, not just confirm it ran.

Beyond aging, Payables ships payment registers covering what was issued over a period, netting reports for business partners offsetting payables against receivables, and income tax and withholding reports for suppliers subject to tax withholding.

And a Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report ties the subledger's view of what's owed and paid to what actually posted in the GL. If those totals don't match during close, something in the subledger-to-GL transfer needs investigation first. Up next, lesson twenty-seven: Receivables reports, aging and collections, the mirror image.
